html:
Chile is a long, narrow country between the Andes and the Pacific, running over four thousand kilometres from the Atacama Desert to Cape Horn. It became independent in 1818.

The Incas reached as far south as central Chile. Beyond them the Mapuche held off the Spanish for three centuries in the Arauco War, so Spanish Chile was a small farming colony in the central valley under the Viceroyalty of Peru. Bernardo O'Higgins and José de San Martín won independence in 1817 and 1818.

Chile built one of the most stable states in 19th century Latin America. In the War of the Pacific of 1879 to 1884 it beat Peru and Bolivia and took the nitrate deserts of the north, leaving Bolivia without a coast. At the same time it conquered the Mapuche lands in the south. Nitrate made Chile rich until synthetic fertiliser killed the trade after the First World War; copper then took its place.

In 1970 Chileans elected the Marxist Salvador Allende. On 11 September 1973 the army overthrew him, and General Augusto Pinochet ruled until 1990. Thousands were killed or tortured, while free market reforms remade the economy. A vote in 1988 ended his rule.

Chile has two Nobel prize winning poets, Gabriela Mistral and Pablo Neruda. It also suffered the strongest earthquake ever recorded, the Valdivia earthquake of 1960.
sum: Chile is a long, narrow country between the Andes and the Pacific, running over four thousand kilometres from the Atacama Desert to Cape Horn. It became independent in 1818.
